request:
Remove speculative unpublished-artifact checks from merge_pr

## Problem

`merge_pr` currently compares the selected local artifact tree with the known Pull Request head tree and refuses to merge when they differ.

This is intended to catch a Graph that produced local changes but forgot to run `sync_pr` first.

That is a speculative correctness guard around Graph authoring. It makes `merge_pr` judge whether the workflow was assembled correctly rather than simply performing the requested merge of the target Pull Request.

## Expected outcome

Keep `merge_pr` focused on the merge operation itself.

Conceptually:

```text
merge_pr
  ↓
identify target Pull Request
  ↓
request merge of its current/known head
  ↓
GitHub accepts or rejects
```

Do not reject the merge because some separate local artifact has unpublished changes unless the merge operation itself requires that comparison for correctness.

If a Graph author wants local changes included in the Pull Request, the Graph should explicitly execute `sync_pr` before `merge_pr`.

Do not add hidden workflow-correctness policy to compensate for a possibly misconfigured Graph.

## Context

The guiding principle is:

> Graph correctness belongs in the Graph, not in speculative System Action safeguards.

GitHub remains authoritative for whether the actual Pull Request can be merged.


User directive: GitWeave implements, creates a separate PR, reviews/fixes iteratively and merges only when clean. Stop on unsupported operations or permission/allowance limits and ask the user. No parent manual substitute is authorized.
